superseded_by.scope: Current strict-resume status for Anima, SDXL and Krea2 full-backbone FP32 computation; all values and timestamps below remain historical evidence.
superseded_by.current_result: Fixed r4 source: uninterrupted 8 steps versus a cold process resume from state 4 to step 8 passed bitwise for 685 Anima, 1680 SDXL and 430 Krea2 weight tensors, all five checkpoint-state categories and preview PNG. Krea2 used two-rank FSDP with 33 FP32 parameter/reduction groups and 14 execution checks per phase.
superseded_by.limits: Recorded BF16 full-backbone failures and Anima/SDXL adapter failures are not rewritten as passed. The r5 integrated product-entry validation is separate; see the newer report for its evidence rather than inferring it from the r4 configuration tests.

limits: Anima and SDXL strict resume remain unresolved; execution and export reload passing do not imply bitwise uninterrupted equivalence.
Full training freezes text encoders. Klein full uses Adafactor; this does not validate full AdamW under the same VRAM budget.
Native export checks call the product sampling worker directly; API scheduling is covered by the separate real multi-GPU product report.

Native Windows single-job multi-GPU training is explicitly rejected by the server, for DDP and FSDP; those modes require Linux CUDA/DTK. Windows installation/switch/uninstall and separate single-GPU jobs assigned to different devices were not exercised in this macOS/Linux DTK setup. DTK acceptance does not establish Windows sharded training support.
Short training and low-step previews establish execution, not convergence, style quality, or long-duration stability.
SDXL independent cold-vs-cold full-model resumes also differ. Only an approved filtered summary of this diagnostic was downloaded; the exact cause remains unresolved.

FSDP2 strict cold-process resume passed on the explicit r2 toy model. Official Krea2 r2 full FSDP capacity/training/resume execution and native reload passed, but strict final equivalence failed for all 430 parameter tensors; cause and long-run impact remain unknown.

r3 adds online-VAE planning and scheduler-contract validation after the r2 formal runs. CPU checks do not establish r3 official-model numerical equivalence; its Toy hardware rerun found a collective-order defect during resume; the original failure report is retained, while a separate repaired r4 Toy cold-process regression passed. This does not rerun official Krea2 or remove its strict failure.

audit.method: Official header only plus actual SingleStreamDiT meta construction and FullTrainingSet; no real tensor allocation or GPU execution
audit.boundary_scope: Existing full backbone training: FP32 parameters and gradients resident on each device; excludes activations, temporaries, communication buckets and optimizer extras. Frozen-only block swapping does not offload trainable full weights.

ypuddin/models/krea2/vendor/krea2_mmdit..reason: Actual SingleStreamDiT architecture matched all official header tensor names and shapes.

ypuddin/train/training_modes.py.reason: FullTrainingSet converts each selected module to float32 and enables gradients on every parameter.

ypuddin/train/trainer.py.reason: Backbone moved to training device; optimizer built over FullTrainingSet parameters.

ypuddin/train/trainer.py#optimizer.reason: Ordinary optimizer.step followed by zero_grad; no per-layer gradient release or CPU optimizer offload.

ypuddin/memory/block_swap.py.reason: Only parameters without requires_grad plus buffers are swappable; all-full meta audit finds zero swappable elements.

ypuddin/train/distributed.py.reason: Each rank runs normal _prepare_training then wraps the full graph in DistributedDataParallel; no parameter sharding/FSDP/ZeRO.

krea2_full_capacity.reason: FP32 parameters and gradients alone require 95.52 GiB per rank, above 64 GiB. DDP does not pool device memory.
krea2_full_capacity.historical_scope_note: This original nonsharded/DDP memory-bound audit remains unchanged. Subsequent actual two-GPU FSDP training is recorded separately under krea2_fsdp_full.
